About Me
item.description:
Profile

I am Yifan Guo, a Robotics undergraduate at Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech). My work spans robotic perception, reinforcement learning, embedded control, and mechanical prototyping.

Education

B.S. in Robotics
Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China | Expected June 2027

  • GPA: 3.77/4.00; average: 90.87/100
  • Relevant coursework: Machine Learning, Control Engineering, Robot Modeling and Control, Mechatronics

Research Experience

Vision-LiDAR Fusion for 3D Target Localization

Built a synchronized perception pipeline combining YOLO, Livox point-cloud projection, clustering, and 2D-3D association. Validation against motion-capture ground truth showed that 95% of detections within 5 m had 3D localization error below 10 cm.

Vision-Based Dexterous-Hand Grasping

Built an Isaac Gym and UniDexGrasp++-based grasp-training pipeline, processed RGB-D observations into point-cloud inputs, debugged Arduino multi-motor control, and deployed trained policies on Jetson Nano Super.

Metamorphic-Structure Reconfigurable Aircraft

Participated in the mechanical and control design of an aircraft that switches between airship and fixed-wing configurations. Built the Gazebo/ROS 2 simulation environment and worked with Pixhawk, QGroundControl, STM32, and Arduino.

Technical Skills

  • Programming: C++, Python, Linux/Ubuntu, Git, Docker, PyTorch
  • Robotics systems: ROS 2, Gazebo, Isaac Gym, Pixhawk, QGroundControl, STM32, Arduino, NVIDIA Jetson
  • Perception: OpenCV, YOLO, RGB-D processing, point-cloud processing, LiDAR-camera calibration, 3D localization
  • Learning and control: Reinforcement learning, robotic grasping, embedded motor control
  • Design: SolidWorks

Honors, Awards, and Funding

item.title: Vision-LiDAR Fusion for 3D Target Localization
item.description:
Project Overview

This project develops a vision-LiDAR fusion pipeline for locating spherical targets in 3D and estimating their motion. It combines image-space object detection with projected LiDAR measurements, turning complementary camera and depth observations into one spatial estimate.

The system is designed for real-time robotic perception rather than offline analysis. A global-shutter camera and Livox LiDAR are hardware-synchronized, while the processing pipeline runs and is tested on NVIDIA Jetson hardware.

What I Built

  • Integrated YOLO-based target detection with LiDAR point-cloud projection.
  • Implemented point-cloud clustering and 2D-3D association between image detections and LiDAR returns.
  • Hardware-synchronized a global-shutter camera and Livox LiDAR.
  • Built a motion-estimation stage from consecutive 3D target observations.
  • Validated localization results against motion-capture ground truth.

Results

For targets within 5 metres, 95% of detections achieved a 3D localization error below 10 cm when evaluated against motion-capture measurements.

Technical Stack

Area Tools / Methods
Detection YOLO, global-shutter camera
3D perception Livox LiDAR, point-cloud projection and clustering
Fusion Camera-LiDAR calibration, 2D-3D association
Deployment NVIDIA Jetson, Python/C++, OpenCV
Validation Motion-capture ground truth

Next Steps

Project images, pipeline diagrams, and demonstration video will be added as the experimental setup is documented.

item.title: Vision-Based Dexterous-Hand Grasping with Reinforcement Learning
item.description:
Project Overview

This project explores vision-guided robotic grasping with a five-finger dexterous hand and a reconfigurable palm. The goal is to connect mechanical hand design, RGB-D perception, reinforcement-learning simulation, and physical motor control in one end-to-end system.

Working with four teammates, I helped establish a training pipeline based on UniDexGrasp++ and prepared the perception and embedded-control components needed for physical validation.

What I Built

  • Contributed to the concept of a five-finger hand with a reconfigurable palm surface.
  • Built an Isaac Gym simulation environment for grasp-policy training.
  • Processed RGB-D observations and back-projected depth maps into point-cloud inputs.
  • Debugged an Arduino-based multi-motor control interface.
  • Deployed trained policies on Jetson Nano Super for physical-system validation.

System Pipeline

The workflow begins with RGB-D observations, converts depth measurements into a spatial point representation, and feeds that representation into the learned grasping policy. Actions produced by the policy are then mapped to the hand’s motor-control interface for simulation and hardware testing.

Technical Stack

Area Tools / Methods
Learning Reinforcement learning, UniDexGrasp++
Simulation Isaac Gym
Perception RGB-D processing, depth back-projection, point clouds
Embedded control Arduino, multi-motor control
Deployment Jetson Nano Super, PyTorch

Project Status

The project received national-level innovation-program support in 2026. Images, simulation recordings, and physical grasping demonstrations will be added in a later update.

item.title: Metamorphic-Structure Reconfigurable Aircraft
item.description:
Project Overview

This project investigates a metamorphic aircraft for long-endurance, low-altitude exploration. The vehicle switches between an airship configuration and a twin-rotor fixed-wing configuration, using a cable-driven winding mechanism to open and close the aircraft frame.

The prototype demonstrates how mechanical transformation, flight-control hardware, and embedded actuation can be integrated into one platform. The work received RMB 20,000 in research funding through the SUSTech Climbing Program.

My Contribution

  • Participated in the mechanical design of the reconfigurable airframe and cable-driven transformation mechanism.
  • Built control and electromechanical actuation systems for configuration switching.
  • Created a Gazebo and ROS 2 simulation environment.
  • Debugged communication between Pixhawk and QGroundControl.
  • Implemented STM32- and Arduino-based motor and servo control.
  • Completed a functional prototype and ground configuration-switching demonstration.

Transformation Concept

The central mechanism uses a winding assembly to coordinate the opening and closing of the airframe. In its expanded state, the structure supports the fixed-wing flight configuration; after folding, it transitions toward the compact airship configuration. The design focuses on proving the mechanical and control concept at prototype scale.

Technical Stack

Area Tools / Methods
Mechanical design SolidWorks, metamorphic structure, cable-driven mechanism
Simulation Gazebo, ROS 2
Flight control Pixhawk, QGroundControl
Embedded control STM32, Arduino, motor and servo actuation
Validation Functional prototype, ground transformation demo

Design Development

The project progressed from structural drawings and mechanism studies to a physical prototype. Iterating between CAD design and hardware assembly helped expose constraints around cable routing, frame synchronization, actuation range, and repeatable configuration switching.

Recognition

  • Chinese invention patent application No. 2026102057666, accepted by CNIPA; co-inventor, third listed.
  • SUSTech Climbing Program research grant: RMB 20,000.

item.title: 8-Legged Biomimetic Robot
item.description:
Project Overview

This demo presents an 8-legged biomimetic robot prototype built to explore stable multi-leg walking, compact mechanical transmission, and low-level motion control. The current version focuses on making the walking gait readable and repeatable before adding more advanced perception or autonomy.

The project is useful as a robotics portfolio piece because it combines physical design, actuator coordination, and embedded software into one visible system. Even from a short video, the viewer can understand the core challenge: turning a set of repeated leg motions into a stable forward gait.

What I Built

  • A physical 8-legged walking mechanism with coordinated leg movement.
  • A basic control pipeline for repeatable stepping and speed adjustment.
  • A prototype test setup for observing gait stability, body vibration, and turning behavior.
  • A media-first project page so the result is visible before the technical details.

Technical Stack

Area Tools / Methods
Mechanical design Linkage structure, leg layout, chassis integration
Control Gait timing, motor coordination, simple feedback tuning
Embedded system Microcontroller-based actuation control
Testing Video observation, gait iteration, stability checks

Design Notes

The robot’s key design problem is rhythm. With eight legs, the system needs a gait pattern that keeps enough contact points on the ground while avoiding visible dragging or fighting between legs. The prototype uses repeated gait cycles so the motion can be tested quickly and improved through mechanical and control adjustments.

Future iterations could add sensor feedback, closed-loop speed control, and a cleaner turning behavior. A later version could also compare multiple gait patterns and visualize their stability on the project page.

item.title: OpenVINS-based UAV Swarm Cooperative Self-Localization System
item.description:
🎯 Project Overview

Solving the drift problem in UAV swarm operations without GPS dependency.

This project implements a comprehensive visual-inertial odometry (VIO) system for UAV swarms, combining OpenVINS, ROS2 communication architecture, and cooperative localization algorithms to achieve high-precision positioning in both simulation and real-world environments.

Tech Stack

  • Middleware: ROS2 (Humble)
  • Programming: C++17, Python
  • VIO Engine: OpenVINS
  • Simulation: Gazebo Sim(Fortress), PX4 SITL
  • Flight Control: PX4 Autopilot, MAVROS
  • Computer Vision: OpenCV, Eigen
  • Optimization: Ceres Solver, g2o
  • Visualization: RViz2

🖥️ Simulation

Gazebo Physical Simulation

We built a high-fidelity simulation environment with:

  • Realistic lighting and shadow rendering
  • Physically accurate UAV dynamics and sensor noise models
  • Multi-UAV spawn system with collision avoidance

Figure: Multi-UAV cooperative exploration in a complex environment

RViz2 Visualization

Our visualization pipeline displays:

  • Trajectory tracking (Path messages with color-coded time series)
  • 3D Point Cloud Maps from stereo vision
  • Real-time pose estimation with uncertainty ellipsoids

Figure: Real-time visualization of UAV poses, trajectories, and point cloud maps

Distributed State Estimation Architecture:

Challenges & Solutions

Challenge 1: ROS2 Cross-Device Communication Latency

Problem: Network latency caused pose updates to arrive 50-100ms late.

Solution:

  • Implemented ZeroMQ-based high-frequency channel for pose data
  • Used ROS2 QoS policies for time-critical messages
  • Achieved < 10ms end-to-end latency

// Custom ZeroMQ publisher for low-latency pose streaming
auto publisher = zmq::socket_t(context, zmq::socket_style::pub);
publisher.bind("tcp://*:5555");

while (rclcpp::ok()) {
 PoseMessage msg = get_latest_pose();
 publisher.send(zmq::buffer(msg.serialize()), zmq::send_flags::none);
}

Challenge 2: IMU Noise Under Vibration

Problem: Motor vibrations caused IMU spikes, degrading VIO accuracy.

Solution:

  • Hardware: Added vibration dampening mounts
  • Software: Adaptive threshold-based outlier rejection
  • Filter: Complementary filter with vibration detection

 2

// Adaptive IMU noise model
double get_adaptive_noise(double vibration_level) {
 return base_noise_ * (1.0 + vibration_gain_ * vibration_level);
}

// Outlier rejection
if (accel_magnitude > threshold) {
 reject_measurement();
 flag_vibration_detected();
}

Challenge 3: Computational Optimization

Problem: OpenVINS processing took 80ms per frame, limiting to 12Hz.

Solution:

  • GPU Acceleration: Ported feature tracking to CUDA
  • Multi-threading: Parallel MSCKF updates for multiple UAVs
  • Code Optimization: SIMD instructions for matrix operations

Performance Improvement:
